title: Add staging integration tests for Console + Optimize SCM calls; fix CI flakes
author: Jada Williams
body: Problem: We’ve had multiple regressions in staging where Console and Optimize clients drifted from Cost Model API behavior (version negotiation, timeouts, and validation). Unit tests cover the SCM library, but we were missing an end-to-end signal that the deployed Console/Optimize services can successfully call SCM in a staging-like environment with real auth, routing, and model-catalog lookups. This PR adds staging integration tests for the SCM call paths used by Console cost breakdown and Optimize “what-if” sweeps, and hardens the CI workflow to reduce flakes we observed in reruns. Summary of changes: (1) New integration test suite `scm_client_staging_it` that runs against the staging Cost Model API and validates `estimate` + `explain` for representative payloads (hosted chat completion, embeddings, and a “what-if” scenario set with batching/caching toggles). (2) Validates version negotiation: requests with `X-Redwood-SCM-Version: 1` and `X-Redwood-SCM-Accept: 1` succeed; requests with unsupported required versions fail with the expected error code and message contract; requests with `Accept` only fall back to v1. (3) Console path coverage: exercises the Console backend adapter (same code path used by the cost breakdown page) with its recommended timeout/retry policy and verifies safe fallback behavior is NOT triggered under healthy conditions; asserts response fields that UI depends on are present (total, breakdown components, assumptions, confidence). (4) Optimize path coverage: runs a small scenario sweep (3 candidates) using the Optimize SCM client, asserting that low-confidence scenarios are surfaced and that recommendation deltas are computed deterministically given fixed inputs. (5) CI flake fixes: adds tenant/test-run isolation (unique `test_run_id` tag), de-races staging tenant provisioning with a bounded exponential backoff, and changes the tests to wait for model-catalog readiness rather than sleeping. Also adds clearer logging on failure (captures request_id + scm_trace_id when present) to speed up triage. Notes on safety: these are non-mutating API calls and run under the existing staging test tenant with read-only cost-model scopes. We intentionally keep payloads small and cap concurrency to avoid load on staging; the suite is gated to `integration-tests-staging` and runs on merge to main + nightly. Test plan: `./tools/test/run_integration --suite scm_client_staging_it --env staging-us-east-1` (manual) and GitHub Actions workflow `staging-integration-tests` (automated). Observed flakes before fixes: ~18% failure rate across reruns, primarily due to transient 503s during rollout windows and race conditions in test tenant bootstrap. After this change and 10 reruns, 0 failures. Follow-ups: A future PR can add a lightweight drift detector comparing `estimate` vs metered attribution for a fixed prompt set once the mismatch detector endpoints stabilize; not included here to keep the staging suite under ~6 minutes.
commits: test(integration): add SCM staging integration test harness and fixtures
console: expose test-only hook to call SCM adapter with staging config
optimize: add minimal scenario sweep runner for staging IT
ci: add bounded retries/backoff + better failure logs for staging IT
ci: wire nightly + post-merge staging integration workflow
test: fix flake by waiting on model-catalog readiness instead of sleep
docs(testing): update internal README for staging integration tests
conversation: Chloe Martin: The Console assertion should match the UI dependency contract; can you assert `assumptions[]` and `confidence.score` are present even when confidence is high? Also please log request_id on failures for Support triage.
Jada Williams (author): Added assertions for `assumptions` and `confidence` fields and improved failure logs to include request_id + scm_trace_id (when available).
Jordan Lee: Version negotiation test should cover the “Accept only” case (no required version) and ensure we actually get v1 back, not just 200 OK. Suggest asserting `schema_version` in payload.
Jada Williams (author): Added `schema_version` assertions and a negative test for unsupported required version returning the expected error code and message prefix.

Hassan Mirza: For Optimize, can we ensure the sweep runner won’t recommend when confidence is low? We’ve had earlier guardrails regress. Add at least one low-confidence fixture and assert it’s flagged.
Jada Williams (author): Added a low-confidence fixture (missing kv_cache_hit_rate) and asserted Optimize marks it non-actionable + includes the confidence explanation in the result log.

Rafael Mendes: Please keep staging load low. Concurrency should be capped, and tests should run nightly + on merge to main, not on every PR by default. Also add jitter to retries to avoid thundering herd.
Jada Williams (author): Capped concurrency to 2, added jitter to backoff, and gated workflow to post-merge + nightly only.
Sean Gallagher: Add a timeout budget per suite and fail fast with a clear message if staging is degraded; otherwise these will burn runner minutes and create noisy alerts.
Jada Williams (author): Added suite-level 8 minute timeout with explicit “staging unhealthy” classification when we see consecutive 503/504 beyond threshold.
Dylan Brooks: Looks good. Once merged, I’ll wire the Console rollout gate to require this check green on main at least once in the last 24h (separate change). Approved.
Merged by Jada Williams using squash merge.
